rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the first experiment should establish a strong reference point for the multimodal pipeline. config_016 combines the most powerful and well-motivated components: multimodal (the study's focus), multiprofile (richer cellular state), scgpt (learned biologically-informed RNA representation), imagenet_vit_l (strongest available image encoder), transformer aggregation (most expressive for multiprofile), and concat fusion (simple, robust baseline). This 'strong prior' configuration tests whether the full multimodal architecture can achieve high accuracy, establishing an upper-bound reference. If it performs well, subsequent experiments can ablate individual components to identify what matters most; if it underperforms, the result flags which dimension to investigate. With 9 experiments remaining, this single informative baseline is the highest-value first move.

With only one completed experiment (config_016: multimodal, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat → 50.7% acc), the most critical uncertainty is whether the multimodal fusion is actually adding value over the image modality alone. The 50.7% accuracy is modest and the F1 (0.455) is notably lower, raising the possibility that the RNA branch is not contributing meaningfully or is introducing noise. config_024 (image_only, multiprofile, imagenet_vit_l, transformer) is the closest single-modality counterpart to config_016, sharing the same image encoder, profile setting, and aggregation. Comparing the two will directly tell us whether the RNA encoder (scgpt) and fusion step are helping or hurting. This baseline is essential before committing remaining budget to multimodal optimization; if image-only matches or exceeds 50.7%, the search should pivot toward image-focused configurations, saving experiments from being wasted on multimodal variants that may not outperform a simpler model.

Evidence: config_016 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) achieved 0.507 accuracy, far exceeding the image-only baseline (config_024, 0.260), confirming that the multimodal setup with scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + transformer is the strongest direction. Question: Does changing the fusion strategy from concat to weighted (config_036) improve upon the best result while keeping all other hyperparameters identical? This is a clean single-variable ablation of the fusion mechanism. Rationale: With 7 experiments remaining, exploiting the strongest evidence with a minimal, interpretable change is the highest-value next step. If weighted fusion helps, it opens a clear optimization axis; if not, it rules out fusion as the next lever and directs attention to RNA encoder or aggregation changes. This avoids over-exploring untested modalities (e.g., RNA-only) that, while scientifically informative, are less likely to yield the best config within the remaining budget.

Evidence: The best result so far is config_036 (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile) at 0.520 acc / 0.479 F1, confirming that multimodal + weighted fusion + ViT-L image encoder is the strongest combination. The RNA encoder axis (scgpt vs scvi_n200 vs pca) remains unexplored under this optimal setting. Question: config_039 swaps scgpt for scvi_n200 while holding all other proven-best components constant (imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile), directly testing whether a VAE-based RNA representation can match or exceed the generative scgpt encoder in a multimodal context. Why this is the best next experiment: With 6 experiments remaining, testing the RNA encoder under the current best architecture is the highest-information move—it either reveals a better RNA representation to exploit in subsequent runs or confirms scgpt as the optimal choice, narrowing the search space significantly for the remaining budget.

The dominant finding is that scvi_n200 as the RNA encoder drives a massive accuracy jump (0.725 in config_039 vs ~0.51-0.52 for scgpt configs), making it the clear backbone. The best config (config_039) uses weighted fusion; the only other scgpt comparison (config_016 vs config_036) showed weighted slightly beating concat, but that was with a weaker RNA encoder. Config_028 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + concat) isolates the fusion method while holding all other components at the best-known values. This tells us whether weighted fusion provides a genuine advantage over concat when the RNA representation is already strong, or whether the ~0.01 gap seen with scgpt was noise. With 5 experiments remaining, understanding which components are truly load-bearing is critical before committing budget to further modifications. If concat matches weighted, it simplifies the search space; if weighted clearly wins, it confirms config_039's fusion choice and we can focus remaining experiments on other axes (aggregation, image encoder).

The current best (config_039, acc=0.725) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted. The dominant factor identified so far is the RNA encoder (scvi_n200 vs scgpt gives ~20% gain), while fusion (weighted vs concat) shows only a ~0.4% difference. The key remaining uncertainty is whether the transformer aggregation is truly necessary or whether a simpler avgpool aggregation performs comparably with the strong scvi_n200 encoder. Config_021 changes exactly one variable from the best (transformer → avgpool, keeping weighted fusion), directly testing whether aggregation architecture matters. This is the best use of experiment 6 because: (1) it is a clean single-variable ablation of the current best, (2) if avgpool matches transformer, it confirms the model is not aggregation-limited and remaining budget can focus on other axes (e.g., image encoder or profile setting); if it falls short, it confirms transformer is essential and we should exploit that. With only 4 experiments left, resolving this uncertainty efficiently is critical.

Evidence: scvi_n200 is the dominant RNA encoder (~0.72 vs ~0.51 for scgpt), and with scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer, weighted fusion (0.725) marginally edges out concat (0.721). The image encoder choice is the largest untested axis under the scvi_n200 regime — all strong results so far use imagenet_vit_l, but we have no direct comparison with resnet50. Question: Does swapping imagenet_vit_l for resnet50 (config_042: scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) maintain or improve performance? This is a clean single-variable ablation against the current best (config_039). Why this is the best use of experiment 7: It directly tests whether the image encoder contributes meaningfully when the RNA encoder is already strong, reducing uncertainty about a key design choice. With 3 experiments remaining, confirming or ruling out resnet50 early lets us either exploit a broader set of resnet50 configs or lock in imagenet_vit_l and focus remaining budget on subtler refinements (e.g., singleprofile, aggregation variants).

The current best (config_039, acc=0.725) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile + transformer + weighted. All top results confirm multiprofile+transformer is strong, but the singleprofile architecture with scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l remains completely untested. Config_007 (singleprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, weighted) isolates the single most important unexplored architectural dimension—whether multiprofile+transformer aggregation is truly necessary or whether a simpler single-profile path with the same strong encoders could match or exceed 0.725. This resolves high uncertainty with the best-known component choices. If it underperforms, it confirms the multiprofile+transformer design and lets the final 2 experiments focus on fine-tuning within that space; if it performs comparably or better, it opens a new promising direction. With only 2 experiments remaining, reducing this architectural uncertainty is the highest-value use of the next slot.

Evidence: The top-4 experiments (config_039: 0.725, config_028: 0.721, config_042: 0.713, config_021: 0.706) establish that scvi_n200 + multiprofile + multimodal is the dominant setting, with imagenet_vit_l > resnet50 and transformer > avgpool, and weighted ≈ concat (small ~0.004 gap). Question: config_018 (scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, concat) completes the 2×2 factorial on image_encoder × fusion under the best aggregation, which is the only cell not yet tested. This clarifies whether the small weighted-over-concat and vit_l-over-resnet50 advantages are purely additive or show interaction effects. Why best use: With only 1 experiment remaining after this, completing the factorial gives the clearest picture of the design space, ensuring the final experiment (if needed) targets a genuine gap rather than a redundant confirmation. It is the most informative remaining scvi_n200 + transformer configuration and the logical extension of the systematic exploration already underway.

Evidence: config_039 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile) achieved the best accuracy at 0.7250, and all top-5 results share multiprofile + transformer aggregation + weighted/concat fusion with scvi_n200. The only untested configuration that pairs the four best-validated settings (imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile) with an alternative RNA encoder is config_041 (pca_n2000). This experiment directly tests whether a simpler linear RNA representation can match or exceed the deep scvi_n200 encoder in the otherwise-optimal pipeline. As the final experiment, it provides a clean ablation (only RNA encoder differs from config_039), confirming whether scvi_n200's ~0.20 accuracy advantage over scgpt is specific to learned representations or generalizable to any non-trivial RNA encoding. This is the highest-value remaining test because it either discovers a competitive alternative or definitively closes the search by validating the best configuration found.
